what: What a person who is not logged in gets when they ask for the list. The plan assumes the safest option, which is no task data and a redirect to the login page. The founder should confirm.?
why: A person who is not logged in gets no task data: every page except login and register redirects to /login (HTTP 302); API-style requests get 401 with no body details.

what: What a member is shown when there are no tasks. The wording of the empty state is not settled.?
why: The empty list shows one line: 'No tasks yet. Add the first one above.' and the add form stays visible.

what: What should happen to a task when an action is interrupted or submitted twice. Done, reopen, reassign and delete are written to be harmless when repeated, but a double-submitted 'add task' could create a duplicate and no rule is set.?
why: Done, reopen, reassign and delete are idempotent: repeating them is harmless and answers the same as the first time. Add task carries a random form token; the server ignores a repeat of the same token within 10 minutes, so a double submit creates one task. A failure midway never leaves a half-written row: each change is one SQLite transaction.

what: Whether 'newest first' for done tasks means newest by completion or newest by creation. The plan uses completion time, kept in one function so it is easy to change.?
why: Newest first by completion time (the moment it was marked done). Reopening clears the completion time.

what: Which accessibility standard, if any, must be met. Step 8 only does basic semantics and labels.?
why: No formal standard. Semantic HTML, a label on every form field, keyboard-operable forms and buttons, readable contrast. Nothing more in version 1.

what: Which privacy rules apply to the stored e-mails and password hashes.?
why: GDPR applies in spirit: store only the e-mail, the display name and the password hash; never log passwords, tokens or e-mails; no third parties; the README says where the data lives and how to delete a member by hand (a command-line script).

what: When the product must be reachable. No availability target or backup schedule is given.?
why: No availability target: it is an internal tool on one machine; if it is down, people wait. Backup: a script `npm run backup` copies the database file to backups/tasks-YYYY-MM-DD.db (the date of the backup); the owner runs it when they want.

what: Hosting is only parked as 'one machine on the local network'. The machine, the port and who looks after it are not confirmed.?
why: One Linux machine on the local network, looked after by the owner. The server listens on PORT (default 3000) on all interfaces; the database file is data/tasks.db (DATABASE_PATH overrides it); both documented in README and .env.example.

what: Whether the local network connection will use HTTPS. Without it, the cookie cannot carry the Secure flag and passwords travel unencrypted on the LAN.?
why: Plain HTTP on the local network, no HTTPS in version 1. The session cookie is httpOnly and SameSite=Lax without the Secure flag; the README states the risk in one sentence and says to put a reverse proxy with TLS in front if the network is not trusted.

what: Password rules (minimum length, etc.) and session lifetime are not given. No numbers have been invented for them.?
why: Password: at least 8 characters, at most 128, no other rules. Session lifetime: 14 days, extended on every request (sliding), and logout deletes the session.

what: How a member who forgot their password gets back in. No reset mechanism is specified, and there is no admin role.?
why: No self-service reset and no e-mail sending. The owner runs a command-line script `npm run set-password -- <email>` on the server machine, which asks for a new password on the terminal and stores its hash.

what: How members are shown in owner pickers. Only the e-mail is collected, and no display name is specified.?
why: A display name is collected at registration (1 to 40 characters, required) and is what members see in owner pickers and task lists; the e-mail is for login only and is never shown to other members.

what: Whether the 11th registrant should see any particular message, and what happens if a registered member is later no longer part of the team. The brief says members are not deleted.?
why: The 11th registration is refused with the message 'This team is full (10 members).' and HTTP 409. Members are never removed in version 1; a member who leaves keeps their account and their tasks can be reassigned.

what: Whether a task's due date can be in the past when it is created or edited. This is not specified.?
why: A due date in the past is allowed on create and edit (someone may record a task that is already late); a task whose due date is before today (the server's local calendar date) and is not done is marked 'overdue' in the list.

what: Whether a member can edit a task's title or due date after creation. The brief only lists reassigning, done, reopen and delete.?
why: Yes: the creator or the current owner can edit a task's title and due date after creation; other members cannot. Title 1 to 200 characters, due date optional, calendar date without time.

what: what should they get?
why: A person who is not logged in gets no task data: every page except login and register redirects to /login (HTTP 302); API-style requests get 401 with no body details.

what: what should a member be shown?
why: The empty list shows one line: 'No tasks yet. Add the first one above.' and the add form stays visible.

what: what should happen to the task?

what: what standard, if any, must it meet?
why: No formal standard. Semantic HTML, a label on every form field, keyboard-operable forms and buttons, readable contrast.

what: which rules apply to the stored e-mails and passwords?
why: Store only the e-mail, the display name and the password hash; never log passwords, tokens or e-mails; no third parties; the README says where the data lives and how to delete a member by hand.

what: when must the product be reachable?
why: No availability target: an internal tool on one machine. Backup by `npm run backup`, which copies the database to backups/tasks-YYYY-MM-DD.db.

what: Is a task's due date required, given the step's NOT NULL test and the problem page say yes but the earlier decision on editing says 'due date optional'?
why: The due date is optional (NULL allowed). The acceptance test and the problem page are to be read as 'every task carries a due date field', which may be empty. Change the step 2 schema and test accordingly.

what: Must display names be unique among members, so two people cannot appear identically in owner pickers?
why: No uniqueness rule for display names; the picker shows 'Name (e-mail local part)' only when two names collide, otherwise just the name.

what: When the owner deletes a member by hand with the command-line script, should the database refuse if that member owns or created tasks, or should those tasks be removed or handed to someone else?
why: The script refuses to delete a member who owns or created tasks and prints how many; it offers a --reassign-to <email> flag that hands the member's tasks to another member first. Nothing is removed silently.

what: After a successful registration, is the new member logged in straight away, or sent to the login page?
why: Logged in straight away after a successful registration and sent to the task list (/).

what: Where does a member land after logging in, and where after logging out, and what does an already logged-in person see when they open the login or register page?
why: After login: the task list (/). After logout: the login page with the line 'You are logged out.' An already logged-in person opening /login or /register is redirected to /.

what: Is the e-mail compared without regard to upper or lower case and with spaces trimmed, and what maximum length and format does it have?
why: E-mail is trimmed and compared lower-cased (stored lower-cased), at most 254 characters, must contain one @ with text on both sides; no stricter format check.

what: What exact wording and HTTP status should the user see for a duplicate e-mail and for a failed login (wrong password or unknown e-mail)?
why: Duplicate e-mail: HTTP 409, 'An account with this e-mail already exists.' Failed login (wrong password or unknown e-mail, same message for both): HTTP 401, 'Wrong e-mail or password.' Both shown on the form with the typed e-mail kept.

what: When the team is already full, does the register page still show the form until it is submitted, or does it show 'This team is full (10 members).' right away?
why: The register page shows 'This team is full (10 members).' right away instead of the form (HTTP 200 on GET); a POST when full is refused with HTTP 409 and the same message.

what: What status and message does a POST with a foreign Origin get, and is a POST with no Origin header allowed or refused?
why: A POST with a foreign Origin gets HTTP 403 and the plain text 'Cross-site request refused.' A POST with no Origin header is allowed (same-origin form posts from old browsers and tests).

what: When a new task is refused (empty title, bad due date, unknown owner), does the member get the form back with their typed values and a specific message for each problem, and with which HTTP status?
why: The member gets the form back with their typed values and one specific message per problem ('Title is required.', 'Due date must be a calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD).', 'Owner must be a member.'), HTTP 400, and the list below it unchanged.

what: Is a title made only of spaces treated as empty, and are spaces at the start and end of a title trimmed before it is stored?
why: Yes: titles are trimmed before validation and storage, and a title made only of spaces is treated as empty.

what: In the owner picker, is the logged-in member preselected as owner, or must the member actively choose someone?
why: The logged-in member is preselected as owner; they can pick someone else.

what: Which details does each open task row show (title, owner's display name, due date, creator), and in what date format is the due date shown?
why: Each open task row shows: title, owner's display name, due date (or 'no due date'), 'overdue' marker when applicable, and 'added by <creator name>'. Dates are shown as YYYY-MM-DD.

what: When a double submit is ignored because the form token was already used, what does the member see: the normal list as after the first add, or a message that the task was already added?
why: The normal list, exactly as after the first add; no message.

what: What exact labels should the buttons on a task row show for marking done and for reopening, for example 'Mark done' and 'Reopen'?
why: 'Mark done' on open tasks and 'Reopen' on done tasks.

what: After a member marks a task done or reopens it, do they land back on the main list, and do they see any confirmation message or just the updated list?
why: They land back on the main list (/), no confirmation message, just the updated list.

what: What should a member see for an unknown or malformed task id: a plain 404 page with set wording, or the list with an error message?
why: A plain 404 page with the text 'Task not found.' (HTTP 404), with a link back to the list.

what: When a task is marked done a second time, should the original completed_at be kept so the order of done tasks doesn't change?
why: Yes: marking done a second time keeps the original completed_at and completed_by; the request succeeds without changing anything.

what: Can a done task be reassigned, or only an open one?
why: Both open and done tasks can be reassigned.

what: Is the reassign control a member picker with a button on each task row, and what is the button's label (for example 'Reassign')?
why: Yes: a member picker (select) with a 'Reassign' button on each task row, open and done.

what: In the reassign picker, is the current owner preselected, or does it start on a 'choose a member' placeholder that must be changed before submitting?
why: The current owner is preselected; submitting with the same owner is a harmless no-op.

what: After a member reassigns a task, where do they land, and do they see a confirmation message (for example 'Reassigned to Sam') or just the updated list?
why: Back on the main list (/), no confirmation message.

what: When a reassign is refused because the chosen person is not a member, what HTTP status and what wording does the member see?
why: HTTP 400 with 'Owner must be a member.' shown above the list; the task is unchanged.

what: What should the Done section show when there are no done tasks yet, for example a heading with a line like 'Nothing done yet.' or no section at all?
why: The Done heading is always shown; when there are no done tasks it shows the line 'Nothing done yet.' under it.

what: In what order are open tasks listed (for example by due date soonest first, or by creation time)?
why: Open tasks: by due date soonest first, tasks without a due date last, ties by creation time oldest first.

what: What does each done task row show besides the title (owner, due date, completion date and time, who completed it), and in what date format?
why: Each done task row shows: title, owner's display name, due date (or 'no due date'), 'done YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM by <name>'. Dates YYYY-MM-DD, times HH:MM in the server's local time.

what: Can the creator delete a done task from the Done section as well as an open one, or only open ones?
why: The creator can delete a task in either state, open or done.

what: Should deleting ask the member to confirm first, and after deleting does the member just return to the list with no message?
why: No confirmation step in version 1 (plain form button); after deleting, the member returns to the list with no message.

what: What exact wording should a member see on the page when they are refused deleting someone else's task with the 403?
why: HTTP 403 with the text 'Only the person who added this task can delete it.' shown above the list.

what: What exact wording and HTTP status should the user see on the generic error page for an unexpected server failure, and on the page for an unknown address?
why: Unexpected failure: HTTP 500 with the text 'Something went wrong. Nothing was saved.' and a link to the list; no stack trace. Unknown address: HTTP 404 with 'Page not found.' and a link to the list.

what: Should an unauthenticated form submission (a POST to a task route) be redirected to /login with a 302 like pages, or refused with a 401?
why: An unauthenticated POST to a task route is refused with HTTP 401 and the text 'Please log in.'; only GET pages redirect with 302.

what: Should repeated failed logins for the same e-mail or from the same address be slowed or temporarily blocked, and if so after how many attempts and for how long?
why: Yes: after 5 failed logins for the same e-mail within 15 minutes, further attempts for that e-mail are refused for 15 minutes with HTTP 429 and 'Too many attempts. Try again in 15 minutes.' Kept in memory, per e-mail only.

what: What HTTP status and message does a member get when they try to delete a task someone else created, since the end-to-end scenario has to check that refusal?
why: HTTP 403 with 'Only the person who added this task can delete it.' (same as step 7).

what: Should the README explain how to restore the database from a backup file, and if so, should it say the server must be stopped first?
why: Yes: the README explains restoring by stopping the server, copying the backup file over data/tasks.db, and starting again. It says the server must be stopped first.

what: Should the README cover keeping the server running, such as starting it again after the machine reboots, or only how to start it by hand with `npm start`?
why: Only how to start it by hand with `npm start`, plus one sentence that a process manager or a systemd unit is up to the owner.

what: Do you want me to edit `gates.yml`?
why: No. Do not edit gates.yml; it is not part of this step. Nothing in the repository registers the protection.

what: What is the exact key or format the harness reads to register protected test files?
why: There is no key to write and nothing to register: the guide protects the acceptance test files itself when this step is done (it records a hash of each test file and refuses later steps that weaken them). Do not add a guard test either. Leave the test file as it is and finish the step.
